clue.text: Fight exists amid calm

indicators.note: amid places the word for exists in the middle of the word for calm

parts.note: rest is calm, repose
is means exists, as in 'there is'

explanation.surface: A paradox: struggle carried on inside a state of tranquillity.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose or withstand something is to fight it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Metal collected by rake, standard procedure

indicators.note: collected by means the metal is gathered up inside the word for rake

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a dissolute man
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Scrap metal gathered with a garden rake as part of a regular chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like the garden tool, but it is the libertine, ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a fixed, habitual way of doing things, a set procedure.

clue.text: Flash 21?

definitions.meaning: an instant, the briefest moment of time
the answer to 21 read word by word: left is to have ... (departed)

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference asking for a flash of the left back.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is LEFT BACK; each word is swapped for a synonym: 'left' as in 'he split', and 'back' as in seconding a motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash is an instant, the shortest moment of time, so the two mean the same.

clue.text: It gets hot on Irish islands, very hot!

parts.note: it is crossword shorthand for sex appeal, SA
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland

explanation.surface: A weather report: it gets hot on the Irish islands, really hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as SA (sex appeal) is an old convention. The Aran Islands are off Galway in western Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Saharan describes desert-like heat, so the adjective is used loosely for scorching weather.

clue.text: Bully has knocked over the Wimbledon favourite — 'e is knocked out!

indicators.note: is knocked out means the letter for 'e is removed
knocked over means the phrase is tipped over and read backwards

parts.note: the favourite at a tennis tournament is the top seed
'e stands for the letter E

explanation.surface: A tennis upset: a bully has beaten the Wimbledon favourite and knocked him out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns TOPSEED into DEESPOT, then 'is knocked out' removes one E, given by ''e'.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a tyrant, someone who rules by intimidation, as a bully does.

clue.text: The liberal state supports one being moral

indicators.note: supports in a down clue puts the state below the letter for one, holding it up
liberal suggests free treatment, so the letters of the word are loosely rearranged

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A political claim that the liberal state backs people in being moral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical and moral both describe conduct that conforms to principles of right and wrong.

clue.text: Friend holding a large potty for attorney's assistant

indicators.note: holding means the word for friend wraps around the rest

parts.note: pal is a friend

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters of large go mad

explanation.surface: A friend clutching a big chamber pot, oddly, for a lawyer's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' is the British word for a child's chamber pot, but here it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A paralegal is a trained worker who supports lawyers without being fully qualified.

clue.text: Land fish, catching two, including first of skate

indicators.note: catching means the fish swallows the rest inside it

parts.note: the tuna is a fish

indicators.note: including means the two numerals enclose a letter

parts.note: two in Roman numerals is II

indicators.note: first of takes only the opening letter of skate

explanation.surface: An angler lands a fish that has caught two others, one a skate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a country, a land in North Africa.

clue.text: Alumnus feeding energetic type a peanut

indicators.note: feeding means the alumnus is put into the mouth of the energetic type

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person
OB is old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil feeding a peanut to a lively friend.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is the usual British term for a school's former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Goober is an American colloquial name for the peanut, from a West African word.

clue.text: Jerk with relations taking drugs? I don't think so!

parts.note: to pull is to jerk or tug
the other is British slang for sex, sexual relations
on E means taking ecstasy, E being the drug

explanation.surface: An incredulous retort to a tale of a jerk with relatives on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of the other' is British slang for sex, so 'relations' gives THE OTHER; 'on E' means high on ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a scoffing reply meaning the speaker does not believe what was just said.

clue.text: Gas worker in better shape

definitions.meaning: someone who installs or repairs gas appliances and pipes
healthier, more athletic, the comparative of fit

explanation.surface: A gas engineer who has got himself into better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a tradesman who fits gas installations and the comparative of fit, healthier.

clue.text: Adverse reaction, as German behind bars injects man with vaccine from behind

indicators.note: injects means the composer takes the other piece into his middle

parts.note: Bach, the German composer, stands behind musical bars

indicators.note: from behind means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Jonas Salk developed the first polio vaccine

explanation.surface: A jailed German injecting a man with vaccine causes an outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind bars' suggests prison, but the bars are musical: the German is BACH. 'from behind' turns SALK into KLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong hostile response from the public to some event or change.

clue.text: German ship to go after the end of four months?

indicators.note: to go after places the ship after the month ending

parts.note: September, October, November and December all end in the same three letters
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German ship due to sail at the close of a four-month period.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native of Berlin, so a German by birth; the word also names a doughnut.

clue.text: Sponsor of art wearing trousers apparently is needing no support?

indicators.note: wearing means the art sponsor is dressed in, so sits inside, the trousers

parts.note: Levi's are a brand of jeans
Henry Tate endowed the Tate gallery of art

explanation.surface: An art patron in trousers apparently floats free without any support.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, funded London's Tate gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rises and hangs in the air does so needing nothing beneath to hold it up.

clue.text: Casual squeezes, say: women's painful experience

indicators.note: squeezes means the word for casual hugs the rest inside

parts.note: lax means casual, careless
eg, for example, is signalled by say
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A casual hug turns into a woman's painful ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot wax pulled from the legs to remove hair is famously an uncomfortable beauty treatment.

clue.text: Note brief question about a formation of flying geese

indicators.note: about means the shortened question goes round the rest
brief means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a query is a question
geese fly in a V shape

explanation.surface: A short question about geese flying in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts QUERY to QUER, and A plus V go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A quaver is a musical note half the length of a crotchet, an eighth note.

clue.text: Type of bend on rather flexible duct

parts.note: a U-bend is a type of bend in a pipe

indicators.note: flexible means the letters of rather bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Plumbing talk: a U-bend fitted on a rather flexible pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges RATHER as RETHRA, under U in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The urethra is the tube carrying urine out of the bladder, an anatomical duct.

clue.text: List including a chicken, perhaps?

indicators.note: including means the list takes the letter in

parts.note: a roster is a list, typically of duties

explanation.surface: A list that seems to include a chicken, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is a bird suitable for roasting, a chicken being the usual example.

clue.text: Lover subsequently put out?

definitions.meaning: a former sweetheart from one's past
read literally, a fire that was later extinguished, now aged and spent

explanation.surface: A lover who was later rejected, or a fire later doused.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is an ex-partner, once burning with passion, now extinguished.

clue.text: Precious thing, important outlying northern island group

parts.note: or is heraldic gold, a precious metal

indicators.note: outlying means the word for important lies around the letter for northern

parts.note: key means important, vital

explanation.surface: Something precious and important found on a remote northern island chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Orkney is an archipelago off the north coast of Scotland, a group of islands.

clue.text: Look down on river holding drinks up

indicators.note: holding means the river encloses the other word

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sips are small drinks

explanation.surface: Gazing down at a river while holding drinks aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the drinks from the bottom upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To despise is to regard with contempt, to look down on someone as inferior.

clue.text: Soldier dressed by setter put on a posh coat

indicators.note: put on in a down clue means the first part sits above the rest
dressed by means the setter clothes the soldier, wrapping round him

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a soldier ant is a type of ant
U is shorthand for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: The setter dresses a soldier, who puts on a smart coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' looks military but is the soldier ant, ANT. U for posh comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A manteau is a loose cloak or gown, an old word for a coat or mantle.

clue.text: Player went to assist

parts.note: left means went away
to back is to support, assist

explanation.surface: A footballer who went off to help a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: A left back is a defender on the left side in football.
explanation.definitionFit: A left back is a defensive position in football, so the term names a player.

clue.text: See 2
Badger starts to chase Himalayan climber

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of the two words that follow

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A badger beginning to chase a mountaineer in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer beside 'Himalayan', but it is the plant IVY.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag or harass them, which is the meaning of chivy.

clue.text: See 26
Ludicrous, a shambles initially among stuff that's contrary

indicators.note: contrary means the word runs the opposite way, back to front
among means the letter goes into the middle of the word for stuff

parts.note: to drub is to defeat, as to stuff an opponent

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of shambles

explanation.surface: Something ludicrous: a total shambles among contrary stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is the slang verb for thrash, DRUB; S goes inside it and 'that's contrary' turns DRUSB into BSURD.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd and ludicrous both mean wildly unreasonable, laughably foolish.

clue.text: 'Oi, you need to explain toughie', he said. By the way, it's impossible!

indicators.note: impossible suggests the words are wrecked into an unrecognisable order

annotation.spelling: HEY YOU WHAT'S THE BIG IDEA

explanation.surface: Someone told to explain a hard puzzle, which by the way cannot be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impossible' rearranges TOUGHIE, HE SAID and BY THE WAY. 'he said' looks like a sound signal; here its letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an indignant challenge demanding someone account for what they are doing.
